sentences.text: The petitioner has approached this Court seeking to quash the notification dated 09.04.2008 (Annexure-A) insofar as it relates to land measuring 6 guntas in Survey No.176/18 situated at Bagaluru Village, Jaala Hobli, Bengaluru North (for short 'the land') and consequently to direct the respondents either to restore the said land notified to the petitioner or, in the alternative to pay the market value as on the date with all statutory benefits.

2. The grievance of the petitioner is that though the subject land was included in the final notification, respondent No.2 had not perused an award in respect thereof and had issued an endorsement that no award has been passed.
3. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has filed a memo producing a copy of the award dated 26.11.2025, which has been approved on 04.12.2025.
4. The same is taken on record.
NC: 2025:KHC:51125 HC-KAR 5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in view of the award having now been passed, the petitioner be reserved liberty to seek enhancement of compensation.

6. Having regard to the above submission and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the award, the writ petition is disposed of with liberty to seek enhancement of compensation, if so advised, in accordance with law.

Sd/-
_____________________ JUSTICE K.S. HEMALEKHA PHM List No.: 1 Sl No.: 2 Sri N Narasimhaiah vs The Government Of Karnataka on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23994052/
